headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Plandex can write/modify git and shell-run in a shared backend, while Whisper is non-writing and local-only, so prompt-injection and leakage are low but coordination errors remain possible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex can ingest files from a project directory and apply staged changes, but Whisper has no text-output or shared-channel surface beyond audio files. There is no documented direct bridge, so prompt injection is only plausible through unusual manual copy/paste or file handoff, not by default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Whisper-transcribed text into Plandex prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared text workspace is introduced between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Whisper outputs in a separate folder from Plandex inputs.
Review any copied transcript before pasting into Plandex.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex for untrusted text.
Use a human approval step before applying generated changes.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex touches source code and can call external model providers, while Whisper is local and has no network egress. The pair does not show a shared filesystem or authenticated workspace, so leakage is limited to operator-mediated transfer of code or transcripts rather than default cross-agent exposure.
conditions: IF source code is copied into Whisper-related tooling, code may be exposed outside Plandex.
IF Whisper transcripts are pasted into Plandex, transcript content becomes visible to Plandex's backend.
mitigations: Do not route source code through Whisper workflows.
Keep transcripts and code in separate directories.
Use local-only handling for both agents where possible.
Redact secrets before any manual transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad shell/network capabilities, while Whisper has no write or shell capability. The conflict is asymmetric, but Plandex's shared backend and multi-instance support mean concurrent Plandex sessions can collide on the same project state; Whisper does not materially reduce that risk.
conditions: IF two Plandex instances target the same repository without locking, writes can conflict.
IF the operator uses auto-apply in Plandex, concurrent state changes become more likely.
mitigations: Run only one Plandex instance per repo at a time.
Avoid auto-apply when multiple sessions exist.
Use git branches for each task.
Pause Whisper-driven workflows before applying Plandex changes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex can generate and apply code changes, and Whisper can produce transcripts that may be fed into Plandex as text. If the operator treats Whisper output as authoritative and Plandex then acts on it without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect code or commits. Whisper itself does not verify facts, so the pair lacks a built-in check.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are used as source material for Plandex plans, transcription errors can propagate.
IF Plandex auto-applies changes derived from unverified transcripts, downstream mistakes can be committed.
mitigations: Verify transcripts against the original audio before use.
Require human review before Plandex apply steps.
Keep transcription outputs labeled as untrusted.
Use small, isolated change sets.

E_compliance.rationale: Plandex handles source code and model-provider API keys, while Whisper handles audio/speech and has no declared secrets or network egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to operator-controlled data placement rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated audio or code is routed through a non-approved environment, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF model-provider keys are stored alongside audio transcripts, retention controls may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools unless approved.
Separate secret storage from transcript storage.
Apply retention rules consistently across repositories.
Document the data class handled by each workflow.
